items.stem: Why is it poor practice to perform a long computation inside an interrupt service routine?

options.text: It blocks other interrupts and increases latency for time-critical events
options.rationale: Correct: a long ISR delays or masks other interrupts, hurting responsiveness.
ISRs can do arithmetic; the issue is how long they run.

options.text: The main loop stops permanently after an interrupt
options.rationale: The main loop resumes after the ISR returns.

options.text: Interrupts automatically disable the CPU clock
options.rationale: Interrupts do not stop the clock.

items.explanation: Correct: a long ISR delays or masks other interrupts, hurting responsiveness.

items.stem: Which TWO signals are required by the I2C bus for communication? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: I2C uses SDA to carry data bits.
Correct: I2C uses SCL to synchronise transfers.

options.text: Separate transmit and receive lines like UART
options.rationale: Those belong to UART, not the two-wire I2C bus.

options.text: A dedicated chip-select line per device like SPI
options.rationale: I2C addresses devices in software, not with chip-select lines.

items.explanation: Correct: I2C uses SDA to carry data bits.

items.stem: A system must react to an external event within 50 microseconds even while busy. Which I/O approach fits best?

options.text: Interrupt-driven I/O, so the event preempts the current work
options.rationale: Correct: interrupts give bounded low-latency response regardless of main-loop work.

options.text: Polling in a slow main loop
options.rationale: Polling latency depends on loop length and may exceed the deadline.

options.text: Disabling all interrupts to save power
options.rationale: Disabling interrupts would prevent the required fast response.

options.text: Adding a delay before checking the input
options.rationale: A delay increases, not decreases, response latency.

items.explanation: Correct: interrupts give bounded low-latency response regardless of main-loop work.
